cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows a full hand-woven strip cloth in a red/orange checkerboard pattern with narrow horizontal weft bands of white, brown, teal and yellow — the classic Ashanti/Ewe kente strip-weaving structure, photographed flat on a neutral background.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Man's cloth (Ewe kente) composed of 21 strips of imported machine cotton, hand-woven and hand sewn together along the selvedges, and arranged in a chequerboard pattern along the cloth without any bands at the ends. The warp design is the same in all the strips, being primarily of green and red stripes, separated by narrower bands of white and brown. The pattern is formed in the weft, with two blocks of orange, blue, yellow, black, green, red and white cotton framing lines and varied patterns between them. There are also broken lines of varied colour running across the sections that show the warp pattern. The cloth is hemmed by hand-sewing.
